extracted.intended_audience: students, critics, and creative writers interested in aesthetics, art history, and literary form
extracted.subtask_description: Critical/aesthetic principles for producing and judging art, poetry, painting, and sculpture according to the Hellenic ideal and its relation to modern art; covers form, temperament, treatment of detail, representation of situation vs type, and the artist's intellectual stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hellenic breadth and generality
rubrics_metrics.description: Hellenic breadth and generality come of a culture minute, severe, constantly renewed, rectifying and concentrating its impressions into certain pregnant types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breadth is not laxity; it is produced by disciplined, minute culture that refines impressions into central types. Evaluate works by whether their generality arises from rigorous refinement rather than from unlearned laxity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of imaginative conception
rubrics_metrics.description: The base of all artistic genius is the power of conceiving humanity in a new, striking, rejoicing way, of putting a happy world of its own creation in place of the meaner world of common days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge creative work by its ability to generate an original imaginative atmosphere that transforms ordinary life—selecting, transforming, recombining images according to an imaginative intellect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastery of the special situation (poetry & painting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Painting and poetry accomplish their function in the choice and development of some special situation, which lifts or glorifies a character, in itself not poetical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the construction of a focused situational moment (example: Robert Browning's dramatic poems). Look for the 'cobweb of allusions' and the artificial light used to make a brief situation apprehensible and ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of cunning subordinate detail and atmosphere
rubrics_metrics.description: To realise this situation... the artist has to employ the most cunning detail, to complicate and refine upon thought and passion a thousand-fold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether details function indirectly and subordinately to build atmosphere and illuminate central motive rather than merely decorate; examples given in painting and Browning's verse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type over situation in sculpture
rubrics_metrics.description: In sculpture, not the special situation, but the type, the general character of the subject to be delineated, is all-important... it effects [power] not by accumulation of detail, but by abstracting from it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For sculptural works, measure success by presentation of broad, central, incisive lines and purified types rather than narrative situations or dense detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purging accidentals; abstraction for clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: All that is accidental, all that distracts the simple effect upon us of the supreme types of humanity, all traces in them of the commonness of the world, it gradually purges away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether an artwork has intentionally removed incidental particulars to reveal a clearer, more universal type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law of limitation and moderation of passion
rubrics_metrics.description: Hellenic generality or breadth... is in every direction a law of limitation; it keeps passion always below that degree of intensity at which it must necessarily be transitory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor works that restrain passion to preserve permanence and repose; avoid one-note extremes of anger, desire, or surprise that become transitory and grotesque.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of the grotesque and single-absorbing-motive faces
rubrics_metrics.description: All such instances may be ranged under the grotesque; and the Hellenic ideal has nothing in common with the grotesque... it allows passion to play lightly over the surface of the individual form, losing thereby nothing of its central impassivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark against works whose figures or faces are fixed into blank, single-motive types (medieval mask-like faces) or that fall into grotesque caricature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restraint in depicted motion and action
rubrics_metrics.description: The archaic immobility has been thawed, its forms are in motion; but it is a motion ever kept in reserve, which is very seldom committed to any definite action... When a more complex and significant action is permitted, it is most often represented as just finished, so that eager expectancy is excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer representations that imply motion or that show an action just completed; avoid eager, unresolved expectancy or over-committed, theatrical action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idealized/sexless purity and delicate transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The beauty of the Greek statues was a sexless beauty... dealing almost exclusively with youth... where the transition from curve to curve is so delicate and elusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge classical-style work by its degree of idealization: sexless purity, youthful modelling, and subtle transitions rather than overt sexualization or coarse detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serenity (Heiterkeit) in handling the sensuous
rubrics_metrics.description: One result of this temperament is a serenity--Heiterkeit--which characterises Winckelmann's handling of the sensuous side of Greek art... it is the absence of any sense of want, or corruption, or shame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether sensuous elements are handled with calm, unashamed detachment (childlike, pagan sensuousness) rather than with guilt, fever, or shameless exhibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calm sensuousness over intoxicated immersion
rubrics_metrics.description: Greek sensuousness, therefore, does not fever the blood; it is shameless and childlike... The artist steeps his thought again and again into the fire of colour. To the Greek this immersion in the sensuous was indifferent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between healthy artistic immersion (colour, sensuous form) that preserves clarity and an intoxicated, ego-consuming immersion that loses intellectual balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-abstraction that leads to corpse-like impassivity
rubrics_metrics.description: The supreme and colourless abstraction of those divine forms... is also a premonition of the fleshless, consumptive refinements of the pale medieval artists... That high indifference to the outward, that impassivity, has already a touch of the corpse in it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warn against abstraction that strips away all life and sensuous interest; abstraction must not produce lifeless, ascetic results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of conflict to avoid ennui
rubrics_metrics.description: But if he was to be saved from the ennui which ever attaches itself to realisation, even the realisation of perfection, it was necessary that a conflict should come, and some sharper note grieve the perfect harmony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value works that introduce conflict or a 'sharper note' to prevent static perfection from becoming boring; conflict should be treated with dignity (example: Greek tragedy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rearrangement of modern detail to satisfy the spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: What modern art has to do in the service of culture is so to rearrange the details of modern life, so to reflect it, that it may satisfy the spirit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For modern subjects, evaluate how effectively an artist restructures chaotic contemporary details into a form that addresses the intellect's need for completeness and centrality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry as form-focused literary production
rubrics_metrics.description: Let us understand by poetry all literary production which attains the power of giving pleasure by its form, as distinct from its matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess literary works by their formal qualities and the pleasure derived from form (language, structure, tonal unity) separately from topical matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of modern necessity as tragic situation
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief factor in the thoughts of the modern mind concerning itself is the intricacy, the universality of natural law... Can art represent men and women in these bewildering toils so as to give the spirit at least an equivalent for the sense of freedom? ... this entanglement, this network of law, becomes the tragic situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge success by how convincingly a work places characters within deterministic social/natural networks and makes that entanglement the basis for tragic development while preserving human dignity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand for unity, centrality, and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: The demand of the intellect is to feel itself alive. It must see into the laws, the operation, the intellectual reward of every divided form of culture... It struggles with those forms till its secret is won from each, and then lets each fall back into its place; in the supreme, artistic view of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate a creative life or work by its ability to achieve unity and centrality—balance of diverse cultural elements into a coherent whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid one-sided specialization; cultivate Allgemeinheit
rubrics_metrics.description: Above all, they are jealous of that abandonment to one special gift which really limits their capabilities... It would have been easy for Goethe... to let it overgrow him... but to the large vision of Goethe, that seemed to be a phase of life that a man might feel all round, and leave behind him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor artists and works that show breadth and general culture rather than narrow, obsessive specialization; value self-cultivation across forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use philosophy as instrument, not dogma
rubrics_metrics.description: "Philosophy is the microscope of thought." The theory or idea or system which requires of us the sacrifice of any part of this experience... has no real claim upon us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess theoretical or philosophical frameworks by whether they help gather and enhance experience; penalize doctrines that demand sacrificing lived experience for abstract conformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursuit of continual sharp observation and novel impressions
rubrics_metrics.description: To burn always with this hard, gemlike flame, to maintain this ecstasy, is success in life... Not to discriminate every moment some passionate attitude... is, on this short day of frost and sun, to sleep before evening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value creative practice and critical attention that continually seek fresh impressions, avoid habitual perception, and maximize intensity of lived moments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passion must quicken consciousness; prefer art for art's sake
rubrics_metrics.description: Great passions may give us this quickened sense of life... the poetic passion, the desire of beauty, the love of art for art's sake, has most; for art comes to you professing frankly to give nothing but the highest quality to your moments as they pass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge works by whether their passions genuinely intensify perception and consciousness; art that exists to heighten the quality of moments is especially valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language purged and layered suggestion in poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: To produce [effects] in a pre-eminent degree requires all the resources of poetry, language in its most purged form, its remote associations and suggestions, its double and treble lights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For poetic/literary evaluation, look for purified language, rich remote associations, and multi-layered suggestiveness rather than prolixity or blunt statement.
